author: Mark Atwood
text:
## Section 7 — Reviewer Calibration

**Maintainer risk:** LOW — the diff is dominated by a mechanically-correct rollout of the workspace extras-preservation policy. Every in-scope type per PLAN.md received the canonical `extra: serde_json::Map` field with `#[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]` and a round-trip preservation test. Every out-of-scope type (filter algebra, capability objects, newtypes, control enums) was correctly excluded with documented rationale. No P0 correctness bugs. All 5 findings are P2 or lower; the workspace-decision finding (.1) is P2 because the divergence between policy doc and code is workspace-wide rather than a local bug.

**Confidence:** ~25% chance of missed bug. Tests pass (`cargo test -p jmap-mail-types --all-features` green; clippy clean under `-D warnings`). The migration is bounded by a clear pre/post-state invariant (every in-scope type round-trips a vendor field).

**Least confident flags:**
- .1 (Unknown vs Other): I asserted the workspace AGENTS.md uses `Unknown(String)` aspirationally and the code uses `Other(String)` universally — verified by grep against jmap-chat-types, jmap-calendars-types, jmap-tasks-types. Did not check jmap-contacts-types, jmap-filenode-types, jmap-sharing-types, jmap-metadata-types. If any of those uses `Unknown(String)` already, the divergence is partial and the decision shape changes.
- .6 (Id vs String key for MdnSendRequest.send): I have not verified the prevailing pattern for client-assigned creation-id keys across the workspace. If `HashMap<String, T>` is canonical in other creation-id contexts, the recommendation reverses.
- .4 (test-coverage gap): the missing test paths (multi-extra, nested-extra, from_str-to_string round-trip) are paths where serde-flatten historically has had bugs, but I did not actually exercise them to confirm any current bug exists. The risk is hypothetical until a specific failure is demonstrated.

**Uncertainty driven by:**
(a) Not running `cargo test --workspace` to confirm sibling crates (jmap-chat-types, jmap-calendars-types, etc.) still compile under the extras-preservation rollout — verified locally for jmap-mail-types only.
(b) Not checking whether `serde(flatten)` on a `Map<String, Value>` has any documented round-trip quirks in serde 1.0.x (changelogs not surveyed).
(c) Not surveying every downstream consumer (jmap-mail-server, jmap-mail-client) to verify their dependence on the public-API shape of the newly-extras'd types — the `extra` field is `pub` and downstream code can in principle construct these maps directly, but I did not check whether jmap-mail-server uses struct-literal syntax that would now require `extra: serde_json::Map::new()`.
(d) Not running cargo public-api or similar to diff the externally-visible SemVer surface of this crate against the pre-9c0d34f state.

**Would raise confidence if:**
1. Ran `cargo test --workspace` and confirmed all sibling crates compile and pass.
2. Ran `cargo public-api diff` between 9c0d34f and HEAD on jmap-mail-types to enumerate the SemVer-visible additions/breakage from the `extra` field rollout.
3. Surveyed jmap-mail-server, jmap-mail-client, jmap-metadata-server, and any other downstream consumer for struct-literal usage of the migrated types that would now require an `extra` field — `#[non_exhaustive]` mostly blocks this, but in-crate uses are not blocked.
4. Spot-checked a representative serde-flatten + Map round-trip in a test harness with two unknown fields + nested array + from_str→to_string to confirm no current serde bug.

**API contract risk:** LOW — the migration is additive in the wire format (empty extras serialize byte-identical to pre-migration; non-empty extras are new wire surface that the policy explicitly wants). `#[non_exhaustive]` on every public struct mostly blocks the API-shape break that the `extra` field could otherwise cause; struct-literal syntax is already unavailable to external callers. The four missing-constructor types (.7) are a pre-existing usability gap; the migration neither closes nor regresses it.

**API contract confidence:** 20% chance of missed issue.

**Idiom rating:** ACCEPTABLE — code is conventional, follows the cookie-cutter template that this crate IS. No unsafe, no .unwrap()/.expect() in library code (all confined to `#[cfg(test)]`), `#[forbid(unsafe_code)]` at crate root, every public struct `#[non_exhaustive]` with documented constructor when one exists. The two real type-design weaknesses (.5 Email::new positional args, .6 send keyed by String) are forward-major-version flags, not present-tense bugs.

**Rust idiom confidence:** ~30% chance of missed issue. The mechanical sameness of the rollout (16 structs receive identical attribute+test pattern) makes idiom violations easy to spot; if I had missed one, it would stand out against the surrounding pattern.

**Bikeshedding flag:** two findings (.5 Email::new positional args, .6 String vs Id key) are labeled `opinion` and have no engineering pressure on the current 0.1.x crate. A /do-beads pass that closes them as wontfix is the right outcome unless the workspace is planning the next major bump. Real findings: 4 (.1, .2, .3, .4, .7).

**bd-review-loop: iter=1 verdict=ok findings=7 p012=4 p3+=3 opinion=2**
